items.title: Invisible and unprotected: India’s new labour codes fail domestic, home-based workers
items.summary: On a blistering afternoon in June, when the temperature had crossed 40 degrees Celsius, 48-year-old Manju (name changed on request) was at home in the dense Mewla Maharajpur locality. She wanted a few minutes of rest before heading out to work as a domestic worker. But the ceiling fan in the room, recirculating hot air, was not helping her cool down. Dreading the blazing sun, Manju reminded herself that it was only a 20-minute-walk to her employer’s home, and that she had been doing this for decades. A few minutes into the walk, she knew something was terribly wrong. “I began to feel overwhelming thirst, followed by a parched throat and nausea. I sat on the side of the road and managed to get drinking water from someone nearby,” she said. Manju’s symptoms indicate that she may have experienced heat exhaustion that arises due to the body's response to an excessive loss of water and salt, usually through profuse sweating. Yet, she did not return home. “I felt guilty about not showing up for work,” said Manju. items.title: Arbitrary power thrives on ignorance, fear: Supreme Court Justice Ujjal Bhuyan
items.summary: Supreme Court Justice Ujjal Bhuyan on Saturday said that scientific temper lays the foundation for the rule of law, since arbitrary power feeds on a society that does not question. A society that stops asking questions becomes vulnerable to authoritarianism, he emphasised. "I believe, scientific temperament lays the foundation for the rule of law. This is because arbitrary power thrives on ignorance, fear and unexamined belief," he said. Thus, a society which believes tradition should be immune from scrutiny will fail to reform unjust practices, he opined. "A society that accepts claims without evidence is susceptible to superstitious beliefs and becomes vulnerable to mis-information. A society that fears questions becomes vulnerable to authoritarianism. A society that treats tradition as beyond scrutiny may fail to reform unjust practices," he said. Justice Bhuyan was delivering the address at the 12th convocation ceremony of the University of Science and Technology Meghalaya (USTM). items.title: ‘Vote Bachao, Desh Bachao’: The INDIA bloc rally at Ramlila Maidan, as it unfolded
items.summary: The INDIA bloc held its “Vote Bachao, Desh Bachao” rally at Ramlila Maidan in Delhi on Sunday. The rally, attended by leaders from across the Opposition, was part of the bloc’s push against the Special Intensive Revision (SIR) of electoral rolls. They had announced that they would walk from Minto Bridge to Ramlila Maidan, but Rahul Gandhi arrived at the venue around 2.30 pm in a vehicle with Akhilesh Yadav and Tejashwi Yadav. At the venue, they addressed the large gathering, as did Mallikarjun Kharge, Mamata Banerjee, Farooq Abdullah, and Mehbooba Mufti. Leaders and attendees demanded the resignation of Chief Election Commissioner Gyanesh Kumar and a rollback of the SIR. Attendees from Bihar, Maharashtra and Rajasthan described voters being left off the rolls despite having documents. Others raised inflation, pollution and women’s safety, showing that the rally was not limited to “vote chori”. Newslaundry spoke to party workers from several states and to ordinary citizens with no party affiliations. items.title: Andhra urban local body polls: Re-polling in 13 stations after booth capture
items.summary: Re-polling is being held in 13 polling stations of seven different urban local bodies in Andhra Pradesh on November 2. The urban local body polls held on November 1 saw many allegations of vote rigging and booth capture allegedly by supporters of the Telugu Desam Party-led coalition government. Four polling stations in Pulivendula municipality were ordered to go for fresh polls as booth capture had taken place, an order from the State Election Commission said on November 1. The counting of votes will happen on November 3. Former chief minister and YSR Congress Party (YSRCP) chief YS Jagan Mohan Reddy had alleged rampant rigging in his constituency Pulivendula and demanded re-polling when he arrived there to cast his vote. His aunt, YS Prameelamma, is the party’s candidate for the post of Pulivendula municipality chairperson. Fresh polls are also being held in one polling station each in Anantapur, Kadapa, and Tirupati municipal corporations, and various polling stations in Macherla, Jammalamadugu, and Chimakurthy municipalities, with the SEC concluding that booth capture had taken place.
